target_customer: consumers who answer and write quiz questions, and sites that embed the widget
problem: Quiz content was scattered; MightyQuiz collected user generated questions that could be answered and rated on site or through a distributable widget.
business_model: unknown; likely advertising supported but no source states it
product_category: user generated quiz platform and embeddable widget

founders.name: Ben Silbermann
founders.role: Founder (2009 to 2010 per his YC profile)
previous_startups: How We Feel (cofounder, per YC profile)
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists him as MightyQuiz founder with a tenure of 2009 to 2010, which is after the Winter 2008 batch.

exit.reason: No shutdown or acquisition announcement found; YC lists the company as Inactive.

competitors.name: HelloQuizzy (OkCupid)
competitors.what: Destination for user generated quizzes plus an engine third party sites could embed

technical_complexity.rationale: A quiz database with ratings and an embeddable widget is standard web engineering for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: User generated content only helps if it reaches scale, and Facebook quiz apps and OkCupid's engine could copy the idea quickly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: HelloQuizzy launched as a spin off within months of the batch; Facebook quiz apps grew fast through 2009.

market_need_then: Quiz content was popular on social networks in 2008, with quiz engines and apps launching that year. Specific demand for MightyQuiz is not documented.

branding.domain_note: mightyquiz.com exact match; the domain now redirects to a domain resale page.

brand_strength.rationale: No press, logo or community material found about the brand.

outcome_analysis: MightyQuiz was a Winter 2008 YC company building user generated quizzes with an embeddable widget. It is now Inactive and no source explains why, so the cause of failure is not public. Quiz engines from OkCupid and many Facebook apps appeared in 2008 and 2009, which is context but not a documented cause.
notes: Only the YC page describes the company. The competitor source is dated three months after the batch start. Silbermann's tenure per the YC profile (2009 to 2010) may mean he joined later than the other founders.
